prompt.context: Your client Maxicure manufactures and sells an over-the-counter cough and cold medicine. Their sole plant in Kentucky is aging, and its increasing maintenance costs are leading to low margins on their products.
prompt.question: How would you advise Maxicure proceed to solve this problem?

clarifying_info.a: There are 2-3 large players in this over-the-counter business who have distribution across the country. Maxicure is one of them.

clarifying_info.q: Where does Maxicure sell its products?
clarifying_info.a: Maxicure sells all of its products in the US.
The objective is to reduce production costs while maintaining product quality. Cost, quality, and brand image all matter to customers.

exhibits.title: Question 2 Data
exhibits.shows: Financial data comparing the in-house build option versus the outsourcing option for Maxicure's manufacturing decision

framework: Identify options available to address the aging plant problem
Evaluate each option on investment cost, per-unit cost, quality impact, capacity/technology improvement, and proximity to distribution centers
Perform break-even analysis between top two options (in-house build vs. outsource)
Consider strategic/political levers such as tax incentives for relocation
Formulate a final recommendation with supporting evidence, risks, and next steps

questions.prompt: What options does Maxicure have for tackling this problem, and what factors would you consider in deciding which option(s) to choose?
questions.guidance: A strong answer identifies all four options (refurbish, rebuild same site, rebuild different location, outsource) and evaluates them on: investment cost, new per-unit cost, financial/non-financial benefits of relocation (e.g. tax breaks, labor rates), effect on medicine quality, opportunity to improve capacity/technology with a new plant, and proximity to distribution centers.

questions.prompt: Maxicure has narrowed down its decision to two options: (1) build a new facility next to the old plant, or (2) outsource manufacturing to a competitor. Using the data provided, how many bottles of medicine would Maxicure need to sell for the in-house option to be more profitable than the outsourcing option?
questions.guidance: Candidate should set up a break-even equation comparing cumulative profits under each option. After the calculation, push the candidate to select a preferred option and give reasons why (e.g. volume outlook vs. 110M threshold, strategic control, quality).

math.setup: Margin in-house = $4.50 - $2.00 = $2.50 per bottle. Margin outsourced (below 20M) = $4.50 - $2.25 = $2.25; (above 20M) = $4.50 - $2.50 = $2.00. In-house has a $50M upfront investment. Set cumulative profit equal at volume x (where x > 20M): In-house profit = 2.5x - 50M. Outsource profit = 2.25*20M + 2.00*(x-20M).
math.answer: Maxicure must sell 110 million bottles for the in-house option to be equally profitable as outsourcing. Above 110M bottles, in-house is more profitable.

questions.prompt: Maxicure has decided to build a new production facility in Indiana to be closer to a major distribution center. How should it convince the Governor of Indiana to offer the necessary tax breaks to make the move more profitable?
questions.guidance: Strong responses should argue from the state's perspective: more tax revenue and economic stimulus, job creation, positive press for the Governor, potential to attract other manufacturers, and community-building initiatives (schools, parks, infrastructure).

questions.prompt: What is your final recommendation to the client?
questions.guidance: Response should follow a structured format: (1) Answer first — state the recommended option clearly. (2) 2-3 pieces of supporting, data-driven evidence (e.g. break-even volume, cost savings, strategic benefits). (3) Key risks (e.g. execution risk, volume uncertainty, quality during transition). (4) Next steps. (5) Re-state the answer.

brainstorming.prompt: How should Maxicure convince the Governor of Indiana to provide tax breaks for the plant relocation?

categories.name: Economic benefits to the state
ideas: Increased tax collection over time as the plant generates revenue
Stimulates local economy through supplier and vendor spending
Higher household income from new jobs boosts local retail and services

categories.name: Job creation
ideas: Direct manufacturing jobs at the new plant
Indirect jobs in supply chain, logistics, and support services

categories.name: Political and reputational benefits
ideas: Good press for the Governor for attracting business
Signals pro-business climate to other companies
Can be used as a campaign success story

categories.name: Broader business attraction
ideas: Might attract other manufacturers looking for similar incentives
Signals Indiana is open to pharmaceutical/healthcare manufacturing

categories.name: Community investment
ideas: Maxicure could commit to building schools or educational facilities
Fund local parks or recreational infrastructure
Partner with local colleges for workforce development programs

recommendation: Build a new production facility in Indiana (next to the old plant site or in Indiana near the distribution center) rather than outsourcing, provided projected sales volume exceeds 110 million bottles
Negotiate tax breaks with the Indiana Governor by presenting the economic, employment, and community benefits of relocation
risks: If actual sales volume falls below 110M bottles, outsourcing would be more profitable — volume projections must be validated
Quality and brand image risk during plant transition period
Execution risk and potential delays in new plant construction
Tax break negotiations may not succeed, affecting the financial case for Indiana relocation
next_steps: Conduct detailed market analysis to validate whether volume will exceed 110M bottles
Engage Indiana economic development office to begin tax incentive negotiations
Commission feasibility study for new plant location and construction timeline
Develop quality assurance plan for transition period to protect brand image
